Output Data and Export

Data and statistics

Statistic Meaning
Count Number of samples
Min / Max Minimum / maximum
Avg Average
Range Max − Min
Std Dev Sample standard deviation
2σ / 3σ Twice / three times the standard deviation

Display precision

Output Data is built from committed ResultRows. Large tables use virtualization for display, but the rows remain available for charts and export.

Number display shares one setting between Summary and Output Data. Auto (default) shows up to 15 significant digits and simplifies floating-point tails; Fixed shows 0–12 decimal places; Raw shows the original JavaScript Number string. Changes apply immediately and carry across Run Pages for the current Desktop session. Count stays an integer, and Elapsed Time/Timestamp formats take priority. These settings do not change stored values, statistics, Charts, exports, or templates.

Statistic selection and limits

Summary shows Count, Min, Max, and Avg by default. Columns ▾ independently controls these columns plus Range (Max − Min), Std Dev (σ), 2σ, and 3σ. Std Dev is the sample standard deviation, calculated as sqrt(M2 / (n - 1)); 2σ and 3σ are its multiples. One sample displays — for all three σ columns, while Range remains available; constant data with at least two samples has Std Dev = 0. For Elapsed time Outputs, Min, Max, Avg, Range, Std Dev, 2σ, and 3σ follow the Output's Time Format from that run, matching Output Data and Scatter X display. Count remains an integer, and missing statistics remain —. Formatting affects display only; the underlying statistics retain their original precision in seconds. Column choices are temporary presentation settings. If a Page has no numeric Outputs, there is no numeric summary to show.

Manual export

Method When and why
Streaming CSV Write data continuously during a run
Manual CSV Export data after execution
Manual XLSX Export an Excel workbook after execution
PNG Export an available chart image
BIN Export raw Serial Background RX bytes
Save Template Save workflow settings, not measured data

Export scope and format

Manual export is available from the Output area after the run is no longer active and the selected export scope contains committed Output rows. Failed or incomplete runs keep their failure/incomplete status and export those committed rows as partial results.

Manual export defaults to XLSX each time the application starts. You can switch between CSV and XLSX during the current session; this choice is not saved. Streaming CSV behavior is unchanged.

Choose Run Page or All Run Pages, then choose CSV or XLSX:

Scope CSV XLSX
Run Page One CSV for the selected Page One worksheet for the selected Page
All Run Pages One CSV per Page in the chosen folder One workbook with a worksheet per Page

Excel time and storage precision

All XLSX time formats use numeric cells suitable for calculations and plotting. Elapsed Seconds stores seconds; the other three formats store seconds / 86400 (Excel days). Timestamp stores the complete date/time serial even when Date is hidden; T and +08:00 are fixed display text. To convert a difference in Excel days to seconds, multiply by 86400. CSV and streaming always retain raw Elapsed seconds and the full ISO Timestamp, regardless of display settings.

Exports use committed ResultRows. XLSX writes finite floating-point values within Excel's supported numeric range as Number cells without rounding stored values, so you can calculate and plot them directly at Excel's native precision (about 15 significant digits). JSON integers retain the existing precision protection; unsafe integers and numbers outside Excel's range remain Text using their stored JSON representation. Numeric-looking strings remain Text; booleans become Boolean cells, null becomes Blank, and arrays/objects remain compact JSON Text. Export preserves stored results; it cannot recover precision already lost when JSON was parsed. Exports do not add formulas or embedded charts. CSV output is unchanged, and All-Pages CSV export does not overwrite existing Page CSV files.

Data from failed or stopped runs

Loop Stop is not itself a failure. Stop Workflow produces a stopped run when cleanup succeeds. After execution stops, rows already committed before a failure or incomplete termination remain eligible for manual export. Rows still staged by a failed or stopped owning scope are not exported.
